courses.title: Philosophy of Medicine
courses.course_description: This course examines the nature, structure and experience of health, disease and illness, focusing on various philosophical and policy issues in biomedical research, theory, and clinical practice. Topics include evidence in clinical trials, bias in medical care, privatized medicine, artificial intelligence in medicine, disability, mental illness, self-narrative in diagnoses, and more. Students will engage major texts and case studies in the history and philosophy of medicine, with the objective of providing a theoretical and philosophical framework for analyzing, evaluating and generating solutions to contemporary debates and experiences relating to health, disease and illness.

courses.title: Ethics of Tech & Communication
courses.course_description: In this course, we will investigate philosophical questions about the nature of technology and communication, as well as ethical questions related to a broad range of specific communication-related technologies. Topics include algorithmic bias and fairness, privacy and surveillance, consent and manipulation, and the environmental impacts of digital technologies. Students will engage with case studies that require applying ethical principles to complex situations.

courses.title: Trustworthy AI
courses.course_description: The course gives an introduction to ethical aspects of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Students learn how concepts, principles, and ethical arguments are used in current debates relating to AI. The focus is on the concept of trustworthy AI and its ethical principles and requirements including respect for human autonomy, prevention of harm, fairness, explicability, safety, privacy and data governance, non-discrimination, transparency, societal and environmental wellbeing, and accountability. The students will learn a use-cased based approach to assess the trustworthiness of AI in practice.
